observations.observation_text: Control procedures are not established which validate the performance of those manufacturing processes that may be responsible for causing variability in the characteristics of in-process material and the drug product. This includes: a lack of assurance that results for in-process physical testing are recorded accurately, as evidenced by incorrect and handwritten specifications on batch records for Hydrocodone Bitartrate and Acetaminophen Tablets, USP 5mg/325mg, Pre-Validation batch record (TB-110); manufacturing investigations into rejected batches of drug products, such as Manufacturing Investigations 04-008 (Batch 310004) and 05-001 (Batch 411021) for Methylphenidate ER 20 mg Tablets, did not include an evaluation of the validated manufacturing process; and no assurance that manufacturing processes for drug products are validated, as out-of-specification (OOS) results were generated but not reported for validation batches, such as Atenolol 25 mg Tablet, Validation Batch 408107A.

evidence_list: Control procedures are not established which validate the performance of those manufacturing processes that may be responsible for causing variability in the characteristics of in-process material and the drug product.

There is no assurance that results for in-process physical testing are recorded accurately. For example, the Pre-Validation batch record (TB-110) for Hydrocodone Bitartrate and Acetaminophen Tablets, USP 5mg/325mg shows the specification for tablet thickness range as 0.308” to 0.358”; this range was crossed out and the correct range of [REDACTION] was handwritten in the batch record.

Manufacturing Investigations into rejected batches of drug products did not include an evaluation of the validated manufacturing process. For example, Manufacturing Investigations, 04-008, for batch 310004, and Manufacturing Investigation 05-001, for batch, 411021 did not include an evaluation of the validated manufacturing process for Methylphenidate ER 20 mg Tablets.

There is no assurance that manufacturing processes for drug products are validated in that out of specification (OOS) results were generated, but not reported. For example, Atenolol 25 mg Tablet, Validation Batch 408107A, Stability Sample 3 mo RT Dissolution, Tablet D5 = 83.7% D6 = 83.8% (OOS), reported D5 = 98.9% D6 = 98.7%.

There is no assurance that results for in-process physical testing are recorded accurately. For example, the Pre-Validation batch record (TB-110) for Hydrocodone Bitartrate and Acetaminophen Tablets, USP 5mg/325mg shows the specification for tablet thickness range as 0.308” to 0.358”; this range was crossed out and the correct range of [REDACTION] was handwritten in the batch record. The in-process tablet thickness results show all tablets were within the corrected thickness specification of [REDACTION] during compression on 10/15/01. The Research and Development (R&D) In-Process Data Sheet shows the thickness of 60 tablets to be within a thickness range of 0.330” and 0.334” which corresponds to the tablet thickness specification which was incorrectly written on the Master Batch Record. Retains from this batch were tested on 6/10/05, and the results show the thickness of the tablets were between [REDACTION] , which was the correct specification that was handwritten on the Master Batch Record. b. Manufacturing Investigations into rejected batches of drug products did not include an evaluation of the validated manufacturing process. For example, seven of nine batches (78%) of Methylphenidate ER 20 mg Tablets, manufactured between May 2003 and November 2004 were investigated in the laboratory, due to initial OOS results or out of trend results. Two of the seven lab investigations, resulted in the rejection of batches 411021 and 310004. Manufacturing Investigations, 04-008, for batch 310004, and Manufacturing Investigation 05-001, for batch, 411021 did not include an evaluation of the validated manufacturing process for Methylphenidate ER 20 mg Tablets. c. There is no assurance that manufacturing processes for drug products are validated in that out of specification (OOS) results were generated, but not reported. Several examples are listed below. 2/12
The quality control unit lacks authority to fully investigate errors that have occurred.
The Quality Unit and Senior Management failed to assure all drug products distributed have the safety, identity, quality, and purity
that they are represented to possess. The Quality Unit failed to: review electronic data as part of batch release, review computer
audit trails in the Waters Empower Data Acquisition System and provide adequate training to analytical chemists. These practices
led to the Quality Unit releasing batches of drug products which failed to meet in­process, finished product and stability
specifications. These practices also led to the submission of erroneous data in Annual Reports and Prior Approval Supplement #
004, for ANDA 75­838, which requested discontinuance of Blend Uniformity testing for Propoxyphene Napsylate and
Acetaminophen 100mg/650 mg Tablets. The lack of Quality oversight resulted in: the ceasing of manufacturing on 5/13/05
5/19/05, the ceasing of distribution of all drug products on 5/26/05 5/13/05, the recall of all batches (3,184) of drug products and
the withdrawal of at least five Abbreviated New Drug Applications.
 
OBSERVATION 2
Drug products failing to meet established standards, specifications, and quality control criteria are not rejected.
Samples of drug products were routinely resampled, and re­injected or reprocessed in the [REDACTION] 
System during testing in the QC Laboratory when out of specification (OOS) results were obtained. There were no Laboratory
Investigations into OOS results or notebook documentation available to explain the re­injection or retesting of in­process, finished
product and stability samples which did not meet specifications. The OOS results were not reported and within specification
results from reprocessed or re­injected samples were reported on: In­Process Specification, Product Specification and Stability
Study Specification Release Reports and Stability Summary Reports.

OBSERVATION 7
Written records are not made of investigations into unexplained discrepancies and the failure of a batch or any of its components
to meet specifications.
Laboratory investigations were not conducted when out of specification (OOS) results were generated during in­process, finished
product and stability testing of drug products. Examples of batches where OOS results were generated and not investigated are
included in FDA­483, point # 2. Quality Control Procedure, SOP # QC­021­06, Acceptance/Rejection Criteria for OOS Analytical
Test Results, requires an investigation be conducted when OOS results are generated.
 
OBSERVATION 8
Employees are not given training in current good manufacturing practices and written procedures required by current good
manufacturing practice regulations.
QC Laboratory analysts were not routinely trained in Quality Control procedures such as SOP # QC­011­03, Laboratory Deviation
Investigations and SOP # QC­021­06, Acceptance/Rejection Criteria for OOS Analytical Test Results. This lack of training and
oversight by management contributed to the non­reporting of OOS results in the QC Laboratory.
 
OBSERVATION 9
Written records of investigations into unexplained discrepancies and the failure of a batch or any of its components to meet
specifications do not always include the conclusions and followup.
OOS Investigation # 04­00S­031, for Methylphenidate HCl ER Tablets 20 mg 18 month stability lot 303087A was initiated due to
dissolution failing results. The specification required the average of 24 tablets to be within the range of [REDACTION] at the L3, 1
hour dissolution time point. The average of the 24 tablets was reported to be 48.4% with a minimum result of 45.8% and a
maximum of 50.2%. The investigation was found to be incomplete. The investigation concluded that the original failing results
were invalid due to an analyst technique issue. There was no documentation provided within the investigation or within the analyst
notebook to justify invalidating the failing dissolution results. Although corrective measures were identified in the investigation,
there was no documentation to show that the corrective measures had been completed. Additionally, there was no review of data
acquired by the same analysts for the same tests for other lots of the same product.

OBSERVATION 11
Established laboratory control mechanisms are not followed.
a. An Investigation was not issued prior to any retesting for Lot 303087B, Methylphenidate HCl ER 18M stability lot, as required
by procedure SOP # QC­011­03, Laboratory Deviation Investigation. Lot 303087B, Methylphenidate HCl ER Tablets 20 mg,
18M Dissolution stability analysis found that the original L3 testing results were within specification. Two months after the
analysis of 24 tablets for Lot 303087B for 18M stability, 6 more tablets were tested. The results from the final analysis of the 6
tablets were reported as 18 M Dissolution results.
b. SOP # QC­006­01 Retesting and Resampling Analytical Control Laboratory, effective 8/27/03 was not followed for
Methylphenidate HCl ER18M stability lot 303087A:
1. There was no documentation of the number of retests to be performed as required by the SOP. The SOP required the
number of retest to be documented prior to initiating testing to establish a definite limit beyond which no additional testing
would be permitted.
2. The procedure required retests to be conducted by the original chemist and a second chemist, where the second
chemist conducts at least 60% of the tests, or by two chemists, neither of which being the chemist producing the original
result. Retests were not carried out by the original chemist and a second chemist. Additionally, the test was not carried
out by two chemists other than the original chemist.
3. Investigation 04­OOS­031, initiated 12/8/04 and completed 2/18/05, exceeded 30 working days. The procedure required
investigations to be completed in a brief time frame not to exceed 30 working days from the start of the investigation.

Control procedures are not established which validate the performance of those manufacturing processes that may be
responsible for causing variability in the characteristics of in­process material and the drug product.
a. There is no assurance that results for in­process physical testing are recorded accurately. For example, the Pre­Validation
batch record (TB­110) for Hydrocodone Bitartrate and Acetaminophen Tablets, USP 5mg/325mg shows the specification for
tablet thickness range as 0.308” to 0.358”; this range was crossed out and the correct range of [REDACTION] was
handwritten in the batch record. The in­process tablet thickness results show all tablets were within the corrected thickness
specification of [REDACTION] during compression on 10/15/01. The Research and Development (R&D) In­Process Data
Sheet shows the thickness of 60 tablets to be within a thickness range of 0.330” and 0.334” which corresponds to the tablet
thickness specification which was incorrectly written on the Master Batch Record. Retains from this batch were tested on
6/10/05, and the results show the thickness of the tablets were between [REDACTION] , which was the correct specification
that was handwritten on the Master Batch Record.
b. Manufacturing Investigations into rejected batches of drug products did not include an evaluation of the validated
manufacturing process. For example, seven of nine batches (78%) of Methylphenidate ER 20 mg Tablets, manufactured
between May 2003 and November 2004 were investigated in the laboratory, due to initial OOS results or out of trend results.

validated manufacturing process for Methylphenidate ER 20 mg Tablets.
c. There is no assurance that manufacturing processes for drug products are validated in that out of specification (OOS) results

observations.observation_text:
(1) The quality control unit lacks the authority and failed to fulfill its responsibilities to assure the safety, identity, quality, and purity of drug products distributed by the firm.

(2) The responsibilities and procedures applicable to the quality control unit are not in writing and/or are not fully followed.
observations.citation_part_label: Part 211—Current Good Manufacturing Practice for Finished Pharmaceuticals
observations.citation_chapter_label: Chapter I—Food and Drug Administration, Department of Health and Human Services
evidence_list: The quality control unit lacks authority to fully investigate errors that have occurred.
The Quality Unit and Senior Management failed to assure all drug products distributed have the safety, identity, quality, and purity that they are represented to possess.

The Quality Unit failed to: review electronic data as part of batch release, review computer audit trails in the Waters Empower Data Acquisition System and provide adequate training to analytical chemists.
These practices led to the Quality Unit releasing batches of drug products which failed to meet in-process, finished product and stability specifications.

These practices also led to the submission of erroneous data in Annual Reports and Prior Approval Supplement # 004, for ANDA 75-838, which requested discontinuance of Blend Uniformity testing for Propoxyphene Napsylate and Acetaminophen 100mg/650 mg Tablets.

The lack of Quality oversight resulted in: the ceasing of manufacturing on 5/13/05 - 5/19/05, the ceasing of distribution of all drug products on 5/26/05 - 5/13/05, the recall of all batches (3,184) of drug products and the withdrawal of at least five Abbreviated New Drug Applications.

Notebook issuance logs showed large gaps in numbering of notebooks issued, which were not accounted for, contrary to SOP # QC-022-04, effective 6/25/04, which specified numerically ordered notebooks would be issued and a log maintained.
The procedure for issuance of notebooks, as described by management (indicating a notebook request form was to be used), was not described in the available procedure.

SOP Method Number I-037, approved 10/18/00, General Guidelines for sample Logging for Analytical Laboratory using [REDACTION] software, did not include procedures and responsibilities for personnel authorized to enter samples into the [REDACTION] database.
Forms required by SOP Method Number I-037 to authorize the addition or deletion of groups, items, samples, and users to the [REDACTION] system were not used.
There was no SOP describing the use of (SP) special samples tested in the Analytical Laboratory, and special samples were not listed as a group in the [REDACTION] procedure.

Special samples, such as SP 04-101 dated 4/24/04 (6 tablets) and SP04-101 dated 4/26/04 (6 tablets) for Methylphenidate HCl ER Tablets 20mg Lot # 303087A 9MRT, were used to report L3 Dissolution results for stability sample #ST04-407 for the same lot.
Dissolution testing for L2 and L3 were not labeled L2 and L3 in the notebook.

evidence_list: Samples of drug products were routinely resampled, and re-injected or reprocessed in the [REDACTION] System during testing in the QC Laboratory when out of specification (OOS) results were obtained.

There were no Laboratory Investigations into OOS results or notebook documentation available to explain the re-injection or retesting of in-process, finished product and stability samples which did not meet specifications.

The OOS results were not reported and within specification results from reprocessed or re-injected samples were reported on: In-Process Specification, Product Specification and Stability Study Specification Release Reports and Stability Summary Reports.

observations.observation_text:
(1) Annual reports and a prior approval supplement submitted to FDA did not include reports of investigations involving chemical or physical properties, specifically out-of-specification (OOS) results, which might affect FDA's previous conclusions about the safety or effectiveness of the drug.

(2) Field Alert Reports were not submitted within three working days of receipt of information concerning a failure of one or more distributed batches of a drug to meet the specifications established for it in the application.

evidence_list: Annual Reports for ANDA’s that were submitted to FDA did not include out of specification (OOS) results. Only passing data points were submitted.
Due to the submission of erroneous data the following ANDA’s were withdrawn: ANDA 75-838, ANDA 40-407, ANDA 76-032, ANDA 40-404.

Examples from Annual Report submitted 8/24/04 for ANDA 75-838: Propoxyphene Napsylate and APAP Tablets, Batch 303110A (Original Dissolution D1=72.8%, D5=73.2%, Reported: D1=98.5%, D5=96.9%); Batch 201016C (Original Assay – Propoxyphene A1=89.9%, Assay – APAP A1=88.7%, Reported: Propoxyphene A1=100.5%, APAP A1=98.9%).

Examples from Annual Report submitted 8/11/04 for ANDA 40-407: Prochlorperazine Suppositories, 2.5 mg, Batch 308029A (Original Unknown Impurities Initial: 0.41% & 0.37%, 6M: 0.28, 0.29 & 0.23%, 9M: 0.32 & 0.33%, Reported: Initial: < 0.01%, 6M: 0.14%, 9M: 0.05%).

Prior Approval Supplement #004 for ANDA 75-838, Propoxyphene Napsylate and APAP Tablets, 100/650mg, submitted on 3/16/04, did not contain initial OOS results for Blend Uniformity and Content Uniformity, only passing results were submitted.

Examples from PAS #004: Batch 312015 (Original Propoxyphene Content Uniformity CU5=117.8%, Reported Range: 102.8% – 108.2%); Batch 310158 (Original Propoxyphene TR1=80.5%, TL1=238.5%, Acetaminophen TL1=218.9%, Reported Range: Propoxyphene 94.7% – 105.2%, APAP 98.5% – 107.7%).
Field Alerts were not routinely filed when drug products did not meet the specifications listed in the Abbreviated New Drug Application (ANDA).
There is no SOP covering the issuance of Field Alerts.

evidence_list: The QC Laboratory notebooks and binders lacked data from all analytical testing conducted in the QC Laboratory.
Laboratory records did not include all data such as out of specification (OOS) results, chromatograms, sample weights, and processing methods.
OOS results were substituted with passing results by Analysts and Supervisors.
The substitution of data was performed by cutting and pasting of chromatograms, substituting vials, changing sample weights and changing processing methods.
For products and batches listed in FDA-483, point # 2, OOS results were not documented in laboratory records but were found in electronic data files.

For Propoxyphene Napsylate and APAP Tablets, Batch 303110A, chromatogram headers were changed by cutting and pasting for Dissolution Testing of Tablets D1 and D5 to make all sample injections appear in sequence.

For Propoxyphene Napsylate and APAP Tablets, Batch 104026B, original sample weights were not recorded in the notebook and were changed by the analyst until a passing result was obtained for Assay (A2).

For Acetaminophen & Codeine Phosphate Tablets, Batch 407148, processing methods were changed by the analyst until a passing result was obtained, and the original processing method was not recorded in the laboratory notebook.

observations.observation_text: Written records of investigations into unexplained discrepancies and the failure of a batch or any of its components to meet specifications are not always made or do not include complete conclusions and followup.
observations.citation_part_label: Part 211—Current Good Manufacturing Practice for Finished Pharmaceuticals

evidence_list: Laboratory investigations were not conducted when out of specification (OOS) results were generated during in-process, finished product and stability testing of drug products, as exemplified by batches listed in FDA-483, point # 2.
Quality Control Procedure, SOP # QC-021-06, Acceptance/Rejection Criteria for OOS Analytical Test Results, requires an investigation be conducted when OOS results are generated.
OOS Investigation # 04-00S-031, for Methylphenidate HCl ER Tablets 20 mg 18 month stability lot 303087A, initiated due to dissolution failing results, was found to be incomplete.

The investigation concluded that the original failing results were invalid due to an analyst technique issue, but no documentation was provided within the investigation or analyst notebook to justify invalidating the results.
Although corrective measures were identified in the investigation, no documentation showed that the corrective measures had been completed.
No review of data acquired by the same analysts for the same tests for other lots of the same product was performed as part of Investigation # 04-00S-031.
observations.source_notes_excerpt: Written records are not made of investigations into unexplained discrepancies and the failure of a batch or any of its components to meet specifications. Laboratory investigations were not conducted when out of specification (OOS) results were generated during in-process, finished product and stability testing of drug products. Examples of batches where OOS results were generated and not investigated are included in FDA-483, point # 2. Quality Control Procedure, SOP # QC-021-06, Acceptance/Rejection Criteria for OOS Analytical Test Results, requires an investigation be conducted when OOS results are generated. Written records of investigations into unexplained discrepancies and the failure of a batch or any of its components to meet specifications do not always include the conclusions and followup. OOS Investigation # 04-00S-031, for Methylphenidate HCl ER Tablets 20 mg 18 month stability lot 303087A was initiated due to dissolution failing results. The specification required the average of 24 tablets to be within the range of [REDACTION] at the L3, 1 hour dissolution time point. The average of the 24 tablets was reported to be 48.4% with a minimum result of 45.8% and a maximum of 50.2%. The investigation was found to be incomplete. The investigation concluded that the original failing results were invalid due to an analyst technique issue. There was no documentation provided within the investigation or within the analyst notebook to justify invalidating the failing dissolution results. Although corrective measures were identified in the investigation, there was no documentation to show that the corrective measures had been completed. Additionally, there was no review of data acquired by the same analysts for the same tests for other lots of the same product.

evidence_list: An investigation was not issued prior to any retesting for Lot 303087B, Methylphenidate HCl ER 18M stability lot, as required by procedure SOP # QC-011-03, Laboratory Deviation Investigation.

For Lot 303087B, Methylphenidate HCl ER Tablets 20 mg, 18M Dissolution stability analysis, original L3 testing results were within specification, but two months after the analysis of 24 tablets, 6 more tablets were tested, and the results from this final analysis were reported as 18M Dissolution results.
SOP # QC-006-01, Retesting and Resampling Analytical Control Laboratory, effective 8/27/03, was not followed for Methylphenidate HCl ER 18M stability lot 303087A:
There was no documentation of the number of retests to be performed prior to initiating testing, as required by the SOP.
Retests were not conducted by the original chemist and a second chemist, nor by two chemists other than the original chemist, as required by the procedure.
Investigation 04-OOS-031, initiated 12/8/04 and completed 2/18/05, exceeded the 30 working days required by the procedure for completion.
observations.source_notes_excerpt: Established laboratory control mechanisms are not followed. a. An Investigation was not issued prior to any retesting for Lot 303087B, Methylphenidate HCl ER 18M stability lot, as required by procedure SOP # QC-011-03, Laboratory Deviation Investigation. Lot 303087B, Methylphenidate HCl ER Tablets 20 mg, 18M Dissolution stability analysis found that the original L3 testing results were within specification. Two months after the analysis of 24 tablets for Lot 303087B for 18M stability, 6 more tablets were tested. The results from the final analysis of the 6 tablets were reported as 18 M Dissolution results. b. SOP # QC-006-01 Retesting and Resampling Analytical Control Laboratory, effective 8/27/03 was not followed for Methylphenidate HCl ER18M stability lot 303087A: 1. There was no documentation of the number of retests to be performed as required by the SOP. The SOP required the number of retest to be documented prior to initiating testing to establish a definite limit beyond which no additional testing would be permitted. 2. The procedure required retests to be conducted by the original chemist and a second chemist, where the second chemist conducts at least 60% of the tests, or by two chemists, neither of which being the chemist producing the original result. Retests were not carried out by the original chemist and a second chemist. Additionally, the test was not carried out by two chemists other than the original chemist. 3. Investigation 04-OOS-031, initiated 12/8/04 and completed 2/18/05, exceeded 30 working days. The procedure required investigations to be completed in a brief time frame not to exceed 30 working days from the start of the investigation.

evidence_list: There is no assurance that results for in-process physical testing are recorded accurately, as demonstrated by the Pre-Validation batch record (TB-110) for Hydrocodone Bitartrate and Acetaminophen Tablets, USP 5mg/325mg, where the tablet thickness specification was incorrectly written on the Master Batch Record and the Research and Development (R&D) In-Process Data Sheet showed results corresponding to the incorrect specification.
Manufacturing Investigations into rejected batches of drug products did not include an evaluation of the validated manufacturing process.

For example, seven of nine batches (78%) of Methylphenidate ER 20 mg Tablets, manufactured between May 2003 and November 2004, were investigated due to initial OOS results or out-of-trend results, with two investigations (04-008 for batch 310004 and 05-001 for batch 411021) resulting in batch rejection, but neither included an evaluation of the validated manufacturing process.

Out-of-specification (OOS) results were generated but not reported for validation batches, indicating a lack of assurance in manufacturing process validation, including Atenolol 25 mg Tablet Validation Batch 408107A (Original Dissolution D5=83.7%, D6=83.8%) and Validation Batch 408107B (Original Dissolution D6=30.9%), and Propoxyphene Napsylate and APAP Tablets Validation Batch 104026B (Original Assay – Propoxyphene A2=89.9%).
observations.source_notes_excerpt: Control procedures are not established which validate the performance of those manufacturing processes that may be responsible for causing variability in the characteristics of in-process material and the drug product. a. There is no assurance that results for in-process physical testing are recorded accurately. For example, the Pre-Validation batch record (TB-110) for Hydrocodone Bitartrate and Acetaminophen Tablets, USP 5mg/325mg shows the specification for tablet thickness range as 0.308” to 0.358”; this range was crossed out and the correct range of [REDACTION] was handwritten in the batch record. The in-process tablet thickness results show all tablets were within the corrected thickness specification of [REDACTION] during compression on 10/15/01. The Research and Development (R&D) In-Process Data Sheet shows the thickness of 60 tablets to be within a thickness range of 0.330” and 0.334” which corresponds to the tablet thickness specification which was incorrectly written on the Master Batch Record. Retains from this batch were tested on 6/10/05, and the results show the thickness of the tablets were between [REDACTION] , which was the correct specification that was handwritten on the Master Batch Record. b. Manufacturing Investigations into rejected batches of drug products did not include an evaluation of the validated manufacturing process. For example, seven of nine batches (78%) of Methylphenidate ER 20 mg Tablets, manufactured between May 2003 and November 2004 were investigated in the laboratory, due to initial OOS results or out of trend results. Two of the seven lab investigations, resulted in the rejection of batches 411021 and 310004. Manufacturing Investigations, 04-008, for batch 310004, and Manufacturing Investigation 05-001, for batch, 411021 did not include an evaluation of the validated manufacturing process for Methylphenidate ER 20 mg Tablets. c. There is no assurance that manufacturing processes for drug products are validated in that out of specification (OOS) results were generated, but not reported. Several examples are listed below. OBSERVATION 1

The quality control unit lacks authority to fully investigate errors that have occurred.
The Quality Unit and Senior Management failed to assure all drug products distributed have the safety, identity, quality, and purity
that they are represented to possess. The Quality Unit failed to: review electronic data as part of batch release, review computer
audit trails in the Waters Empower Data Acquisition System and provide adequate training to analytical chemists. These practices
led to the Quality Unit releasing batches of drug products which failed to meet in­process, finished product and stability
specifications. These practices also led to the submission of erroneous data in Annual Reports and Prior Approval Supplement #
004, for ANDA 75­838, which requested discontinuance of Blend Uniformity testing for Propoxyphene Napsylate and
Acetaminophen 100mg/650 mg Tablets. The lack of Quality oversight resulted in: the ceasing of manufacturing on 5/13/05
5/19/05, the ceasing of distribution of all drug products on 5/26/05 5/13/05, the recall of all batches (3,184) of drug products and
the withdrawal of at least five Abbreviated New Drug Applications.
 
OBSERVATION 2
Drug products failing to meet established standards, specifications, and quality control criteria are not rejected.
Samples of drug products were routinely resampled, and re­injected or reprocessed in the [REDACTION] 
System during testing in the QC Laboratory when out of specification (OOS) results were obtained. There were no Laboratory
Investigations into OOS results or notebook documentation available to explain the re­injection or retesting of in­process, finished
product and stability samples which did not meet specifications. The OOS results were not reported and within specification
results from reprocessed or re­injected samples were reported on: In­Process Specification, Product Specification and Stability
Study Specification Release Reports and Stability Summary Reports.

Written records are not made of investigations into unexplained discrepancies and the failure of a batch or any of its components

Laboratory investigations were not conducted when out of specification (OOS) results were generated during in­process, finished

manufacturing practice regulations.

Written records of investigations into unexplained discrepancies and the failure of a batch or any of its components to meet

OOS Investigation # 04­00S­031, for Methylphenidate HCl ER Tablets 20 mg 18 month stability lot 303087A was initiated due to
dissolution failing results. The specification required the average of 24 tablets to be within the range of [REDACTION] at the L3, 1
hour dissolution time point. The average of the 24 tablets was reported to be 48.4% with a minimum result of 45.8% and a
maximum of 50.2%. The investigation was found to be incomplete. The investigation concluded that the original failing results
were invalid due to an analyst technique issue. There was no documentation provided within the investigation or within the analyst
notebook to justify invalidating the failing dissolution results. Although corrective measures were identified in the investigation,
there was no documentation to show that the corrective measures had been completed. Additionally, there was no review of data
acquired by the same analysts for the same tests for other lots of the same product.

Established laboratory control mechanisms are not followed.
a. An Investigation was not issued prior to any retesting for Lot 303087B, Methylphenidate HCl ER 18M stability lot, as required

18M Dissolution stability analysis found that the original L3 testing results were within specification. Two months after the
analysis of 24 tablets for Lot 303087B for 18M stability, 6 more tablets were tested. The results from the final analysis of the 6
tablets were reported as 18 M Dissolution results.
b. SOP # QC­006­01 Retesting and Resampling Analytical Control Laboratory, effective 8/27/03 was not followed for
Methylphenidate HCl ER18M stability lot 303087A:
1. There was no documentation of the number of retests to be performed as required by the SOP. The SOP required the
number of retest to be documented prior to initiating testing to establish a definite limit beyond which no additional testing
would be permitted.
2. The procedure required retests to be conducted by the original chemist and a second chemist, where the second
chemist conducts at least 60% of the tests, or by two chemists, neither of which being the chemist producing the original
result. Retests were not carried out by the original chemist and a second chemist. Additionally, the test was not carried
out by two chemists other than the original chemist.
3. Investigation 04­OOS­031, initiated 12/8/04 and completed 2/18/05, exceeded 30 working days. The procedure required
investigations to be completed in a brief time frame not to exceed 30 working days from the start of the investigation.

responsible for causing variability in the characteristics of in­process material and the drug product.
a. There is no assurance that results for in­process physical testing are recorded accurately. For example, the Pre­Validation
batch record (TB­110) for Hydrocodone Bitartrate and Acetaminophen Tablets, USP 5mg/325mg shows the specification for
tablet thickness range as 0.308” to 0.358”; this range was crossed out and the correct range of [REDACTION] was
handwritten in the batch record. The in­process tablet thickness results show all tablets were within the corrected thickness
specification of [REDACTION] during compression on 10/15/01. The Research and Development (R&D) In­Process Data

(1) The quality control unit lacks authority to fully investigate errors that have occurred and failed to assure all drug products distributed have the safety, identity, quality, and purity that they are represented to possess.

(2) The responsibilities and procedures applicable to the quality control unit are not in writing and fully followed.

evidence_list: The quality control unit lacks authority to fully investigate errors that have occurred.
The Quality Unit and Senior Management failed to assure all drug products distributed have the safety, identity, quality, and purity that they are represented to possess.

The lack of Quality oversight resulted in: the ceasing of manufacturing on 5/13/05 - 5/19/05, the ceasing of distribution of all drug products on 5/26/05 - 5/13/05, the recall of all batches (3,184) of drug products and the withdrawal of at least five Abbreviated New Drug Applications.

The Laboratory Records SOP # QC-022-04 effective 6/25/04, specified numerically ordered notebooks will be issued and a log maintained. Notebook issuance logs showed large gaps in numbering of notebooks issued, which were not accounted for in the log.
The procedure for issuance of notebooks, as described by management, which indicated a notebook request form was to be used, was not described in the procedure available.

SOP Method Number I-037, approved 10/18/00, General Guidelines for sample Logging for Analytical Laboratory using [REDACTION] software did not include procedures and responsibilities to be followed by personnel authorized to enter samples into the [REDACTION] database.
Forms to be used to authorize the addition or deletion of groups, items, samples, and users to the [REDACTION] system as specified by the SOP were not used.

evidence_list: Drug products failing to meet established standards, specifications, and quality control criteria are not rejected.
Samples of drug products were routinely resampled, and re-injected or reprocessed in the [REDACTION] System during testing in the QC Laboratory when out of specification (OOS) results were obtained.

There were no Laboratory Investigations into OOS results or notebook documentation available to explain the re-injection or retesting of in-process, finished product and stability samples which did not meet specifications.

The OOS results were not reported and within specification results from reprocessed or re-injected samples were reported on: In-Process Specification, Product Specification and Stability Study Specification Release Reports and Stability Summary Reports.

Examples of drug products released with OOS values include: Acetaminophen & Codeine Phosphate Tablet, Batch 502022 (In-Process Blend Uniformity Testing, Codeine Phosphate % RSD: 5.4, reported as 3.8%); Atenolol 25 mg Tablet, Validation Batch 408107B (Stability Sample 3 mo RT, Dissolution Testing Tablet D6 = 30.9%, reported as 102.8%); Propoxyphene Napsylate and APAP Tablets, 100/650mg, Batch 310158 (In-Process Blend Uniformity Testing, Propoxyphene TL1 = 238.5%, TR1 = 80.5%, reported as 103.2% and 104.0% respectively).
Laboratory investigations were not conducted when out of specification (OOS) results were generated during in-process, finished product and stability testing of drug products.
OOS Investigation # 04-00S-031, for Methylphenidate HCl ER Tablets 20 mg 18 month stability lot 303087A, was found to be incomplete.

The investigation concluded that the original failing results were invalid due to an analyst technique issue, but there was no documentation provided within the investigation or within the analyst notebook to justify invalidating the failing dissolution results.
There was no review of data acquired by the same analysts for the same tests for other lots of the same product.
Although corrective measures were identified in the investigation, there was no documentation to show that the corrective measures had been completed.

observations.observation_text:
(1) Annual reports and a prior approval supplement submitted to FDA did not include reports of investigations involving chemical or physical properties which, as new information, might affect FDA's previous conclusions about the safety or effectiveness of the drug, by only submitting passing data points and omitting initial out-of-specification (OOS) results.

(2) Field Alert Reports were not submitted within three working days of receipt of information concerning a failure of one or more distributed batches of a drug to meet the specifications established for it in the application. Additionally, there is no Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) covering the issuance of Field Alerts.

evidence_list: Annual Reports for ANDA’s that were submitted to FDA did not include out of specification (OOS) results. Only passing data points were submitted.
Due to the submission of erroneous data the following ANDA’s were withdrawn.

Annual Report submitted 8/24/04, for reporting period 7/12/03 through 7/11/04, for Propoxyphene Napsylate and APAP Tablets, 100/650mg, Batch 303110A (ANDA 75-838), Stability Sample 12 mo RT, showed Dissolution Tablet D1 = 72.8%, D5 = 73.2% (OOS), but reported D1 = 98.5%, D5 = 96.9%.

Annual Report submitted 11/6/02, for reporting period 7/11/01 through 7/11/02, for Propoxyphene Napsylate and APAP Tablets, 100/650mg, Batch 104026B (ANDA 75-838), Stability Sample 6 mo RT, showed Assay – Propoxyphene A2 = 89.9% (OOS), but reported A2 = 95.9%.

Prior Approval Supplement #004 for ANDA 75-838, Propoxyphene Napsylate and APAP Tablets, 100/650mg, submitted on 3/16/04, did not contain initial OOS results for Blend Uniformity and Content Uniformity testing for a number of batches, only passing results were submitted.

Examples from Prior Approval Supplement #004 include: Batch 312015, Finished product Content Uniformity, Propoxyphene: CU5 = 117.8% (OOS), but reported range 102.8% – 108.2%; Batch 310158, In-process Blend Uniformity, Propoxyphene: TR1 = 80.5%, TL1 = 238.5% (OOS), but reported range 94.7% – 105.2%.
Field Alerts were not routinely filed when drug products did not meet the specifications listed in the Abbreviated New Drug Application (ANDA).
There is no SOP covering the issuance of Field Alerts.

Field Alerts were not submitted when the following batches of drug products failed to meet stability specifications: Atenolol 25 mg Tablet, Validation Batch 408107A (ANDA 76-907), Stability Sample 3 mo RT, Dissolution D5 = 83.7%, D6 = 83.8% (failing result); Diphenoxylate HCl and Atropine Sulfate Tablet, Batch 301068A (ANDA 40-395), Stability Sample 21 mo RT, Assay – Atropine A1 = 78.4%, A2 = 78.7% (failing result); Prochlorperazine Suppositories, 2.5 mg, Batch 308029A (ANDA 40-407), Stability Sample 12 mo RT, Unknown Impurities 0.52%, 0.73% (failing result).

evidence_list: The QC Laboratory notebooks and binders lacked data from all analytical testing conducted in the QC Laboratory.
Laboratory records did not include all data such as out of specification (OOS) results, chromatograms, sample weights, and processing methods.

OOS results were substituted with passing results by Analysts and Supervisors. The substitution of data was performed by cutting and pasting of chromatograms, substituting vials, changing sample weights and changing processing methods.

For Propoxyphene Napsylate and APAP Tablets, 100/650mg, Batch 303110A, chromatogram headers were changed by cutting and pasting to make all sample injections appear in sequence for Dissolution Testing of Tablets D1 and D5.

For Propoxyphene Napsylate and APAP Tablets, 100/650mg, Batch 104026B, original sample weights were not recorded in the notebook; sample weights were changed by the analyst until a passing result was obtained for Assay (A2).

For Acetaminophen & Codeine Phosphate Tablets, 300/30mg, Batch 407148, processing methods were changed by the analyst until a passing result was obtained, and the original processing method was not recorded in the laboratory notebook.

evidence_list: There was no SOP describing the use of (SP) special samples tested in the Analytical Laboratory. Additionally, special samples were not listed as a group in the [REDACTION] procedure.

Special samples (e.g., Methylphenidate HCl ER Tablets 20mg Lot # 303087A 9MRT SP 04-101 dated 4/24/04 (6 tablets) and SP04-101 (6 tablets) dated 4/26/04) were used to report L3 Dissolution results for stability sample #ST04-407 for the same lot, and dissolution testing for L2 and L3 were not labeled L2 and L3 in the notebook.
An Investigation was not issued prior to any retesting for Lot 303087B, Methylphenidate HCl ER 18M stability lot, as required by procedure SOP # QC-011-03, Laboratory Deviation Investigation.

SOP # QC-006-01 Retesting and Resampling Analytical Control Laboratory, effective 8/27/03, was not followed for Methylphenidate HCl ER18M stability lot 303087A, as there was no documentation of the number of retests to be performed prior to initiating testing.

The retests for Methylphenidate HCl ER18M stability lot 303087A were not carried out by the original chemist and a second chemist, or by two chemists other than the original chemist, as required by SOP # QC-006-01.
Investigation 04-OOS-031, initiated 12/8/04 and completed 2/18/05, exceeded the 30 working days timeframe required by the procedure.

18M Dissolution stability analysis found that the original L3 testing results were within specification. Two months after the
analysis of 24 tablets for Lot 303087B for 18M stability, 6 more tablets were tested. The results from the final analysis of the 6
tablets were reported as 18 M Dissolution results.
b. SOP # QC-006-01 Retesting and Resampling Analytical Control Laboratory, effective 8/27/03 was not followed for
Methylphenidate HCl ER18M stability lot 303087A:
1. There was no documentation of the number of retests to be performed as required by the SOP. The SOP required the
number of retest to be documented prior to initiating testing to establish a definite limit beyond which no additional testing
would be permitted.
2. The procedure required retests to be conducted by the original chemist and a second chemist, where the second
chemist conducts at least 60% of the tests, or by two chemists, neither of which being the chemist producing the original
result. Retests were not carried out by the original chemist and a second chemist. Additionally, the test was not carried
out by two chemists other than the original chemist.
3. Investigation 04-OOS-031, initiated 12/8/04 and completed 2/18/05, exceeded 30 working days. The procedure required
investigations to be completed in a brief time frame not to exceed 30 working days from the start of the investigation.

evidence_list: There is no assurance that results for in-process physical testing are recorded accurately. For example, the Pre-Validation batch record (TB-110) for Hydrocodone Bitartrate and Acetaminophen Tablets, USP 5mg/325mg, showed an incorrect tablet thickness specification range (0.308” to 0.358”) which was crossed out and a corrected range of [REDACTION] was handwritten. The R&D In-Process Data Sheet showed the thickness of 60 tablets to be within the incorrectly written range (0.330” and 0.334”), while retains from this batch tested on 6/10/05 showed thickness between [REDACTION], corresponding to the corrected specification.

Manufacturing Investigations into rejected batches of drug products did not include an evaluation of the validated manufacturing process. For example, Manufacturing Investigations 04-008 (for batch 310004) and 05-001 (for batch 411021) for Methylphenidate ER 20 mg Tablets, which were rejected due to initial OOS or out-of-trend results, did not include an evaluation of the validated manufacturing process.

There is no assurance that manufacturing processes for drug products are validated in that out of specification (OOS) results were generated, but not reported, for validation batches such as Atenolol 25 mg Tablet Validation Batch 408107A (Dissolution D5 = 83.7%, D6 = 83.8% OOS, reported as 98.9%, 98.7%) and Propoxyphene Napsylate and APAP Tablets, 100/650mg, Validation Batch 104026B (Assay – Propoxyphene A2 = 89.9% OOS, reported as 95.9%).
observations.source_notes_excerpt:
Control procedures are not established which validate the performance of those manufacturing processes that may be
responsible for causing variability in the characteristics of in-process material and the drug product.
a. There is no assurance that results for in-process physical testing are recorded accurately. For example, the Pre-Validation
batch record (TB-110) for Hydrocodone Bitartrate and Acetaminophen Tablets, USP 5mg/325mg shows the specification for
tablet thickness range as 0.308” to 0.358”; this range was crossed out and the correct range of [REDACTION] was
handwritten in the batch record. The in-process tablet thickness results show all tablets were within the corrected thickness
specification of [REDACTION] during compression on 10/15/01. The Research and Development (R&D) In-Process Data
Sheet shows the thickness of 60 tablets to be within a thickness range of 0.330” and 0.334” which corresponds to the tablet
thickness specification which was incorrectly written on the Master Batch Record. Retains from this batch were tested on
6/10/05, and the results show the thickness of the tablets were between [REDACTION] , which was the correct specification
that was handwritten on the Master Batch Record.
b. Manufacturing Investigations into rejected batches of drug products did not include an evaluation of the validated
manufacturing process. For example, seven of nine batches (78%) of Methylphenidate ER 20 mg Tablets, manufactured
between May 2003 and November 2004 were investigated in the laboratory, due to initial OOS results or out of trend results.
Two of the seven lab investigations, resulted in the rejection of batches 411021 and 310004. Manufacturing Investigations,
04-008, for batch 310004, and Manufacturing Investigation 05-001, for batch, 411021 did not include an evaluation of the
validated manufacturing process for Methylphenidate ER 20 mg Tablets.
c. There is no assurance that manufacturing processes for drug products are validated in that out of specification (OOS) results

audit trails in the Waters Empower Data Acquisition System and provide adequate training to analytical chemists. These practices
led to the Quality Unit releasing batches of drug products which failed to meet in­process, finished product and stability
specifications. These practices also led to the submission of erroneous data in Annual Reports and Prior Approval Supplement #
004, for ANDA 75­838, which requested discontinuance of Blend Uniformity testing for Propoxyphene Napsylate and
Acetaminophen 100mg/650 mg Tablets. The lack of Quality oversight resulted in: the ceasing of manufacturing on 5/13/05
5/19/05, the ceasing of distribution of all drug products on 5/26/05 5/13/05, the recall of all batches (3,184) of drug products and
the withdrawal of at least five Abbreviated New Drug Applications.
 
OBSERVATION 2
Drug products failing to meet established standards, specifications, and quality control criteria are not rejected.
Samples of drug products were routinely resampled, and re­injected or reprocessed in the [REDACTION] 
System during testing in the QC Laboratory when out of specification (OOS) results were obtained. There were no Laboratory
Investigations into OOS results or notebook documentation available to explain the re­injection or retesting of in­process, finished
product and stability samples which did not meet specifications. The OOS results were not reported and within specification
results from reprocessed or re­injected samples were reported on: In­Process Specification, Product Specification and Stability
Study Specification Release Reports and Stability Summary Reports.

(1) The quality control unit lacks the authority to fully investigate errors and has failed to assure the safety, identity, quality, and purity of distributed drug products, leading to significant regulatory actions including the recall of 3,184 batches and withdrawal of at least five Abbreviated New Drug Applications.

(2) The responsibilities and procedures applicable to the quality control unit are not in writing and fully followed, including procedures for laboratory records, sample logging, and the use of special samples.

observations.source_notes_excerpt:
The Quality Unit failed to: review electronic data as part of batch release, review computer
audit trails in the Waters Empower Data Acquisition System and provide adequate training to analytical chemists. These practices
led to the Quality Unit releasing batches of drug products which failed to meet in­process, finished product and stability
specifications. These practices also led to the submission of erroneous data in Annual Reports and Prior Approval Supplement #
004, for ANDA 75­838, which requested discontinuance of Blend Uniformity testing for Propoxyphene Napsylate and
Acetaminophen 100mg/650 mg Tablets. The lack of Quality oversight resulted in: the ceasing of manufacturing on 5/13/05
5/19/05, the ceasing of distribution of all drug products on 5/26/05 5/13/05, the recall of all batches (3,184) of drug products and
the withdrawal of at least five Abbreviated New Drug Applications.

evidence_list: Established laboratory control mechanisms are not followed.
An Investigation was not issued prior to any retesting for Lot 303087B, Methylphenidate HCl ER 18M stability lot, as required by procedure SOP # QC-011-03, Laboratory Deviation Investigation.
SOP # QC-006-01 Retesting and Resampling Analytical Control Laboratory, effective 8/27/03 was not followed for Methylphenidate HCl ER18M stability lot 303087A:
There was no documentation of the number of retests to be performed as required by the SOP.

The procedure required retests to be conducted by the original chemist and a second chemist, where the second chemist conducts at least 60% of the tests, or by two chemists, neither of which being the chemist producing the original result. Retests were not carried out by the original chemist and a second chemist. Additionally, the test was not carried out by two chemists other than the original chemist.

Investigation 04-OOS-031, initiated 12/8/04 and completed 2/18/05, exceeded 30 working days. The procedure required investigations to be completed in a brief time frame not to exceed 30 working days from the start of the investigation.

1. There was no documentation of the number of retests to be performed as required by the SOP. The SOP required the

would be permitted.
2. The procedure required retests to be conducted by the original chemist and a second chemist, where the second
chemist conducts at least 60% of the tests, or by two chemists, neither of which being the chemist producing the original
result. Retests were not carried out by the original chemist and a second chemist. Additionally, the test was not carried
out by two chemists other than the original chemist.

evidence_list: Control procedures are not established which validate the performance of those manufacturing processes that may be responsible for causing variability in the characteristics of in-process material and the drug product.
There is no assurance that results for in-process physical testing are recorded accurately.

the Pre-Validation batch record (TB-110) for Hydrocodone Bitartrate and Acetaminophen Tablets, USP 5mg/325mg shows the specification for tablet thickness range as 0.308” to 0.358”; this range was crossed out and the correct range of [REDACTION] was handwritten in the batch record.

The Research and Development (R&D) In-Process Data Sheet shows the thickness of 60 tablets to be within a thickness range of 0.330” and 0.334” which corresponds to the tablet thickness specification which was incorrectly written on the Master Batch Record.
Manufacturing Investigations into rejected batches of drug products did not include an evaluation of the validated manufacturing process.

seven of nine batches (78%) of Methylphenidate ER 20 mg Tablets, manufactured between May 2003 and November 2004 were investigated in the laboratory, due to initial OOS results or out of trend results.

Manufacturing Investigations, 04-008, for batch 310004, and Manufacturing Investigation 05-001, for batch, 411021 did not include an evaluation of the validated manufacturing process for Methylphenidate ER 20 mg Tablets.

OBSERVATION 12
Control procedures are not established which validate the performance of those manufacturing processes that may be
responsible for causing variability in the characteristics of in­process material and the drug product.
a. There is no assurance that results for in­process physical testing are recorded accurately. For example, the Pre­Validation
batch record (TB­110) for Hydrocodone Bitartrate and Acetaminophen Tablets, USP 5mg/325mg shows the specification for
tablet thickness range as 0.308” to 0.358”; this range was crossed out and the correct range of [REDACTION] was
handwritten in the batch record. The in­process tablet thickness results show all tablets were within the corrected thickness
specification of [REDACTION] during compression on 10/15/01. The Research and Development (R&D) In­Process Data
Sheet shows the thickness of 60 tablets to be within a thickness range of 0.330” and 0.334” which corresponds to the tablet
thickness specification which was incorrectly written on the Master Batch Record. Retains from this batch were tested on
6/10/05, and the results show the thickness of the tablets were between [REDACTION] , which was the correct specification
that was handwritten on the Master Batch Record.
b. Manufacturing Investigations into rejected batches of drug products did not include an evaluation of the validated
manufacturing process. For example, seven of nine batches (78%) of Methylphenidate ER 20 mg Tablets, manufactured
between May 2003 and November 2004 were investigated in the laboratory, due to initial OOS results or out of trend results.
Two of the seven lab investigations, resulted in the rejection of batches 411021 and 310004. Manufacturing Investigations,
04­008, for batch 310004, and Manufacturing Investigation 05­001, for batch, 411021 did not include an evaluation of the
validated manufacturing process for Methylphenidate ER 20 mg Tablets.
c. There is no assurance that manufacturing processes for drug products are validated in that out of specification (OOS) results
were generated, but not reported. Several examples are listed below.

2/12
The quality control unit lacks authority to fully investigate errors that have occurred.
The Quality Unit and Senior Management failed to assure all drug products distributed have the safety, identity, quality, and purity
that they are represented to possess. The Quality Unit failed to: review electronic data as part of batch release, review computer
audit trails in the Waters Empower Data Acquisition System and provide adequate training to analytical chemists. These practices
led to the Quality Unit releasing batches of drug products which failed to meet in­process, finished product and stability
specifications. These practices also led to the submission of erroneous data in Annual Reports and Prior Approval Supplement #
004, for ANDA 75­838, which requested discontinuance of Blend Uniformity testing for Propoxyphene Napsylate and
Acetaminophen 100mg/650 mg Tablets. The lack of Quality oversight resulted in: the ceasing of manufacturing on 5/13/05
5/19/05, the ceasing of distribution of all drug products on 5/26/05 5/13/05, the recall of all batches (3,184) of drug products and
the withdrawal of at least five Abbreviated New Drug Applications.
 
OBSERVATION 2
Drug products failing to meet established standards, specifications, and quality control criteria are not rejected.
Samples of drug products were routinely resampled, and re­injected or reprocessed in the [REDACTION] 
System during testing in the QC Laboratory when out of specification (OOS) results were obtained. There were no Laboratory
Investigations into OOS results or notebook documentation available to explain the re­injection or retesting of in­process, finished
product and stability samples which did not meet specifications. The OOS results were not reported and within specification
results from reprocessed or re­injected samples were reported on: In­Process Specification, Product Specification and Stability
Study Specification Release Reports and Stability Summary Reports.

OOS Investigation # 04­00S­031, for Methylphenidate HCl ER Tablets 20 mg 18 month stability lot 303087A was initiated due to
dissolution failing results. The specification required the average of 24 tablets to be within the range of [REDACTION] at the L3, 1
hour dissolution time point. The average of the 24 tablets was reported to be 48.4% with a minimum result of 45.8% and a
maximum of 50.2%. The investigation was found to be incomplete. The investigation concluded that the original failing results
were invalid due to an analyst technique issue. There was no documentation provided within the investigation or within the analyst
notebook to justify invalidating the failing dissolution results. Although corrective measures were identified in the investigation,
there was no documentation to show that the corrective measures had been completed. Additionally, there was no review of data
acquired by the same analysts for the same tests for other lots of the same product.

Dissolution testing for L2 and L3 were not labeled L2 and L3 in the notebook.
 
OBSERVATION 11
Established laboratory control mechanisms are not followed.
a. An Investigation was not issued prior to any retesting for Lot 303087B, Methylphenidate HCl ER 18M stability lot, as required
by procedure SOP # QC­011­03, Laboratory Deviation Investigation. Lot 303087B, Methylphenidate HCl ER Tablets 20 mg,
18M Dissolution stability analysis found that the original L3 testing results were within specification. Two months after the
analysis of 24 tablets for Lot 303087B for 18M stability, 6 more tablets were tested. The results from the final analysis of the 6
tablets were reported as 18 M Dissolution results.
b. SOP # QC­006­01 Retesting and Resampling Analytical Control Laboratory, effective 8/27/03 was not followed for
Methylphenidate HCl ER18M stability lot 303087A:
1. There was no documentation of the number of retests to be performed as required by the SOP. The SOP required the
number of retest to be documented prior to initiating testing to establish a definite limit beyond which no additional testing
would be permitted.
2. The procedure required retests to be conducted by the original chemist and a second chemist, where the second
chemist conducts at least 60% of the tests, or by two chemists, neither of which being the chemist producing the original
result. Retests were not carried out by the original chemist and a second chemist. Additionally, the test was not carried
out by two chemists other than the original chemist.
3. Investigation 04­OOS­031, initiated 12/8/04 and completed 2/18/05, exceeded 30 working days. The procedure required
investigations to be completed in a brief time frame not to exceed 30 working days from the start of the investigation.
Production System
 
OBSERVATION 12
Control procedures are not established which validate the performance of those manufacturing processes that may be
responsible for causing variability in the characteristics of in­process material and the drug product.
a. There is no assurance that results for in­process physical testing are recorded accurately. For example, the Pre­Validation
batch record (TB­110) for Hydrocodone Bitartrate and Acetaminophen Tablets, USP 5mg/325mg shows the specification for
tablet thickness range as 0.308” to 0.358”; this range was crossed out and the correct range of [REDACTION] was
handwritten in the batch record. The in­process tablet thickness results show all tablets were within the corrected thickness
specification of [REDACTION] during compression on 10/15/01. The Research and Development (R&D) In­Process Data
Sheet shows the thickness of 60 tablets to be within a thickness range of 0.330” and 0.334” which corresponds to the tablet
thickness specification which was incorrectly written on the Master Batch Record. Retains from this batch were tested on
6/10/05, and the results show the thickness of the tablets were between [REDACTION] , which was the correct specification
that was handwritten on the Master Batch Record.
b. Manufacturing Investigations into rejected batches of drug products did not include an evaluation of the validated
manufacturing process. For example, seven of nine batches (78%) of Methylphenidate ER 20 mg Tablets, manufactured
between May 2003 and November 2004 were investigated in the laboratory, due to initial OOS results or out of trend results.
Two of the seven lab investigations, resulted in the rejection of batches 411021 and 310004. Manufacturing Investigations,
04­008, for batch 310004, and Manufacturing Investigation 05­001, for batch, 411021 did not include an evaluation of the
validated manufacturing process for Methylphenidate ER 20 mg Tablets.
c. There is no assurance that manufacturing processes for drug products are validated in that out of specification (OOS) results

observations.observation_text:
(1) The Quality Control Unit lacks the authority to fully investigate errors and fails to ensure that all distributed drug products possess the required safety, identity, quality, and purity. This includes failures to review electronic data and computer audit trails as part of batch release, and to provide adequate training to analytical chemists, leading to the release of non-conforming products and submission of erroneous data to the FDA.

(2) The responsibilities and procedures applicable to the quality control unit are not in writing and fully followed. This includes deficiencies in the issuance and logging of laboratory notebooks, lack of procedures for personnel authorized to enter samples into the [REDACTION] database, and absence of an SOP describing the use of special samples, leading to inadequate control over laboratory operations and data integrity.

These practices led to the Quality Unit releasing batches of drug products which failed to meet in-process, finished product and stability specifications. The lack of Quality oversight resulted in: the ceasing of manufacturing on 5/13/05 5/19/05, the ceasing of distribution of all drug products on 5/26/05 5/13/05, the recall of all batches (3,184) of drug products and the withdrawal of at least five Abbreviated New Drug Applications. | OBSERVATION 10 The responsibilities and procedures applicable to the quality control unit are not in writing and fully followed. a. Instead, samples are routinely re-sampled, re-injected, or reprocessed in the QC Laboratory when out-of-specification (OOS) results are obtained, without proper investigation or documentation. observations.observation_text:
(1) Annual reports and prior approval supplements submitted to the FDA did not include reports of investigations involving chemical or physical properties, specifically out-of-specification (OOS) results, which might affect FDA's previous conclusions about the safety or effectiveness of the drug. Only passing data points were submitted, leading to the withdrawal of multiple Abbreviated New Drug Applications (ANDAs).

(2) Field Alert Reports are not submitted within three working days of receiving information concerning a failure of one or more distributed batches of a drug to meet established specifications. The firm lacks a Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for the issuance of Field Alerts, and multiple batches of drug products failed to meet stability specifications without Field Alerts being filed.

observations.observation_text: Laboratory records do not include complete data derived from all tests, examinations, and assays necessary to assure compliance with established specifications and standards. Out-of-specification (OOS) results, chromatograms, sample weights, and processing methods are not fully documented. Analysts and supervisors substitute OOS results with passing results by manipulating data, such as cutting and pasting chromatograms, substituting vials, changing sample weights, and altering processing methods for various drug products and batches.

Laboratory investigations are not conducted when out-of-specification (OOS) results are generated, and when investigations are initiated, they lack sufficient documentation to justify conclusions and do not include documentation of completed corrective measures or review of data from other lots by the same analysts.

observations.source_notes_excerpt: OBSERVATION 7 Written records are not made of investigations into unexplained discrepancies and the failure of a batch or any of its components to meet specifications. Laboratory investigations were not conducted when out of specification (OOS) results were generated during in-process, finished product and stability testing of drug products. Examples of batches where OOS results were generated and not investigated are included in FDA-483, point # 2. Quality Control Procedure, SOP # QC-021-06, Acceptance/Rejection Criteria for OOS Analytical Test Results, requires an investigation be conducted when OOS results are generated. OBSERVATION 9 Written records of investigations into unexplained discrepancies and the failure of a batch or any of its components to meet specifications do not always include the conclusions and followup. OOS Investigation # 04-00S-031, for Methylphenidate HCl ER Tablets 20 mg 18 month stability lot 303087A was initiated due to dissolution failing results. The specification required the average of 24 tablets to be within the range of [REDACTION] at the L3, 1 hour dissolution time point. The average of the 24 tablets was reported to be 48.4% with a minimum result of 45.8% and a maximum of 50.2%. The investigation was found to be incomplete. The investigation concluded that the original failing results were invalid due to an analyst technique issue. There was no documentation provided within the investigation or within the analyst notebook to justify invalidating the failing dissolution results. Although corrective measures were identified in the investigation, there was no documentation to show that the corrective measures had been completed. Additionally, there was no review of data acquired by the same analysts for the same tests for other lots of the same product.

This includes failing to issue investigations prior to retesting, not documenting the number of retests to be performed, not ensuring retests are conducted by appropriate personnel, and exceeding the required timeframe for investigation completion, as observed for Methylphenidate HCl ER Tablets stability lots.

evidence_list: Established laboratory control mechanisms are not followed.
An Investigation was not issued prior to any retesting for Lot 303087B, Methylphenidate HCl ER 18M stability lot, as required by procedure SOP # QC-011-03, Laboratory Deviation Investigation.

Two months after the analysis of 24 tablets for Lot 303087B for 18M stability, 6 more tablets were tested. The results from the final analysis of the 6 tablets were reported as 18 M Dissolution results.
SOP # QC-006-01 Retesting and Resampling Analytical Control Laboratory, effective 8/27/03 was not followed for Methylphenidate HCl ER18M stability lot 303087A
There was no documentation of the number of retests to be performed as required by the SOP.
The SOP required the number of retest to be documented prior to initiating testing to establish a definite limit beyond which no additional testing would be permitted.

The procedure required retests to be conducted by the original chemist and a second chemist, where the second chemist conducts at least 60% of the tests, or by two chemists, neither of which being the chemist producing the original result.
Retests were not carried out by the original chemist and a second chemist.
Additionally, the test was not carried out by two chemists other than the original chemist.
Investigation 04-OOS-031, initiated 12/8/04 and completed 2/18/05, exceeded 30 working days.
The procedure required investigations to be completed in a brief time frame not to exceed 30 working days from the start of the investigation.
observations.source_notes_excerpt: OBSERVATION 11 Established laboratory control mechanisms are not followed. a. An Investigation was not issued prior to any retesting for Lot 303087B, Methylphenidate HCl ER 18M stability lot, as required by procedure SOP # QC-011-03, Laboratory Deviation Investigation. Lot 303087B, Methylphenidate HCl ER Tablets 20 mg, 18M Dissolution stability analysis found that the original L3 testing results were within specification. Two months after the analysis of 24 tablets for Lot 303087B for 18M stability, 6 more tablets were tested. The results from the final analysis of the 6 tablets were reported as 18 M Dissolution results. b. SOP # QC-006-01 Retesting and Resampling Analytical Control Laboratory, effective 8/27/03 was not followed for Methylphenidate HCl ER18M stability lot 303087A: 1. There was no documentation of the number of retests to be performed as required by the SOP. The SOP required the number of retest to be documented prior to initiating testing to establish a definite limit beyond which no additional testing would be permitted. 2. The procedure required retests to be conducted by the original chemist and a second chemist, where the second chemist conducts at least 60% of the tests, or by two chemists, neither of which being the chemist producing the original result. Retests were not carried out by the original chemist and a second chemist. Additionally, the test was not carried out by two chemists other than the original chemist. 3. Investigation 04-OOS-031, initiated 12/8/04 and completed 2/18/05, exceeded 30 working days. The procedure required investigations to be completed in a brief time frame not to exceed 30 working days from the start of the investigation.

observations.source_notes_excerpt: Production System OBSERVATION 12 Control procedures are not established which validate the performance of those manufacturing processes that may be responsible for causing variability in the characteristics of in-process material and the drug product. a. There is no assurance that results for in-process physical testing are recorded accurately. For example, the Pre-Validation batch record (TB-110) for Hydrocodone Bitartrate and Acetaminophen Tablets, USP 5mg/325mg shows the specification for tablet thickness range as 0.308” to 0.358”; this range was crossed out and the correct range of [REDACTION] was handwritten in the batch record. The in-process tablet thickness results show all tablets were within the corrected thickness specification of [REDACTION] during compression on 10/15/01. The Research and Development (R&D) In-Process Data Sheet shows the thickness of 60 tablets to be within a thickness range of 0.330” and 0.334” which corresponds to the tablet thickness specification which was incorrectly written on the Master Batch Record. Retains from this batch were tested on 6/10/05, and the results show the thickness of the tablets were between [REDACTION] , which was the correct specification that was handwritten on the Master Batch Record. b. Manufacturing Investigations into rejected batches of drug products did not include an evaluation of the validated manufacturing process. For example, seven of nine batches (78%) of Methylphenidate ER 20 mg Tablets, manufactured between May 2003 and November 2004 were investigated in the laboratory, due to initial OOS results or out of trend results. Two of the seven lab investigations, resulted in the rejection of batches 411021 and 310004. Manufacturing Investigations, 04-008, for batch 310004, and Manufacturing Investigation 05-001, for batch, 411021 did not include an evaluation of the validated manufacturing process for Methylphenidate ER 20 mg Tablets. c. There is no assurance that manufacturing processes for drug products are validated in that out of specification (OOS) results were generated, but not reported. Several examples are listed below. Quality System
OBSERVATION 1

6/24/2016

The quality control unit lacks authority to fully investigate errors that have occurred.
The Quality Unit and Senior Management failed to assure all drug products distributed have the safety, identity, quality, and purity
that they are represented to possess. The Quality Unit failed to: review electronic data as part of batch release, review computer
audit trails in the Waters Empower Data Acquisition System and provide adequate training to analytical chemists. These practices
led to the Quality Unit releasing batches of drug products which failed to meet in­process, finished product and stability
specifications. These practices also led to the submission of erroneous data in Annual Reports and Prior Approval Supplement #
004, for ANDA 75­838, which requested discontinuance of Blend Uniformity testing for Propoxyphene Napsylate and
Acetaminophen 100mg/650 mg Tablets. The lack of Quality oversight resulted in: the ceasing of manufacturing on 5/13/05
5/19/05, the ceasing of distribution of all drug products on 5/26/05 5/13/05, the recall of all batches (3,184) of drug products and
the withdrawal of at least five Abbreviated New Drug Applications.
 
OBSERVATION 2
Drug products failing to meet established standards, specifications, and quality control criteria are not rejected.
Samples of drug products were routinely resampled, and re­injected or reprocessed in the [REDACTION] 
System during testing in the QC Laboratory when out of specification (OOS) results were obtained. There were no Laboratory
Investigations into OOS results or notebook documentation available to explain the re­injection or retesting of in­process, finished
product and stability samples which did not meet specifications. The OOS results were not reported and within specification
results from reprocessed or re­injected samples were reported on: In­Process Specification, Product Specification and Stability
Study Specification Release Reports and Stability Summary Reports.

acquired by the same analysts for the same tests for other lots of the same product.

a. There is no assurance that results for in­process physical testing are recorded accurately. For example, the Pre­Validation
batch record (TB­110) for Hydrocodone Bitartrate and Acetaminophen Tablets, USP 5mg/325mg shows the specification for
tablet thickness range as 0.308” to 0.358”; this range was crossed out and the correct range of [REDACTION] was
handwritten in the batch record. The in­process tablet thickness results show all tablets were within the corrected thickness
specification of [REDACTION] during compression on 10/15/01. The Research and Development (R&D) In­Process Data
Sheet shows the thickness of 60 tablets to be within a thickness range of 0.330” and 0.334” which corresponds to the tablet
thickness specification which was incorrectly written on the Master Batch Record. Retains from this batch were tested on
6/10/05, and the results show the thickness of the tablets were between [REDACTION] , which was the correct specification
that was handwritten on the Master Batch Record.
b. Manufacturing Investigations into rejected batches of drug products did not include an evaluation of the validated
manufacturing process. For example, seven of nine batches (78%) of Methylphenidate ER 20 mg Tablets, manufactured
between May 2003 and November 2004 were investigated in the laboratory, due to initial OOS results or out of trend results.
Two of the seven lab investigations, resulted in the rejection of batches 411021 and 310004. Manufacturing Investigations,

validated manufacturing process for Methylphenidate ER 20 mg Tablets.
c. There is no assurance that manufacturing processes for drug products are validated in that out of specification (OOS) results

Specifically, the Quality Unit failed to review electronic data and computer audit trails as part of batch release and did not provide adequate training to analytical chemists. These practices led to the release of drug products that failed specifications and the submission of erroneous data in Annual Reports and a Prior Approval Supplement.
